title: LLMShare: Optimizing LLM Inference Serving with Hardware Architecture Exploration
problem: LLM serving systems use fixed hardware configurations that don't differentiate between the prefill phase (high parallelism, compute-bound) and decoding phase (low parallelism, memory-bandwidth-bound), leading to resource waste and high serving costs.
motivation: The prefill and decoding phases have radically different computational and bandwidth characteristics; optimizing for one degrades the other, so systems need heterogeneous hardware tailored to each phase.
method: Develops a simulator modeling performance and cost across heterogeneous hardware configurations (CPUs, GPUs, accelerators), then applies design space exploration to find the Pareto-optimal allocation of resources to prefill vs. decoding stages. Aligns hardware capabilities with specific phase demands.
key_novelty: Systematic design space exploration framework that treats prefill and decoding as separately optimizable hardware phases rather than forcing a one-size-fits-all solution.
contributions: Simulator for performance and cost across heterogeneous LLM serving hardware
Design space exploration framework for phase-specific hardware allocation
13% cost savings and 4× throughput improvements over conventional setups
limitations: Evaluation limited to existing hardware products; no custom ASIC results; scalability to very large model sizes not discussed.
primary_theme: phase-aware hardware partitioning for LLM inference
